anomaly_def.Name: Database Configuration Parameter Anomaly + Transaction Log Subsystem Anomaly + Operating System Resource Limit Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Database Configuration Parameter Anomaly: Engine-level settings (memory, checkpoint cadence, log sizing, parallelism, etc.) are mis-tuned relative to hardware capacity, workload intensity, or version defaults.
Transaction Log Subsystem Anomaly: The write-ahead logging pipeline—log buffer, files, flush/switch/archive processes—cannot keep pace with redo generation, stalling commits and checkpoints.
Operating System Resource Limit Anomaly: Kernel-enforced ceilings on file handles, shared memory, threads, or I/O contexts throttle database processes independently of the engine’s internal resource governance.

When these three issues strike concurrently, symptoms overlap and amplify: commit latency and log-flush waits spike even though storage and CPU appear under-utilized; checkpoints and log-file switches occur in erratic bursts, sometimes failing with "unable to open file" or shared-memory allocation errors; background writers, archivers, and replication senders fall behind, causing bloated log directories and prolonged recovery point objectives; new sessions or parallel workers intermittently fail to start, and the engine may enter a partial hang where active transactions linger in commit wait while resource-starved background tasks cannot progress. Performance counters show low device saturation but high wait times on log and kernel primitives, confusing first-level diagnostics.

Causally, mis-sized configuration parameters (e.g., too small log buffer, aggressive checkpoint_timeout, excessive max_connections) inflate the churn on the transaction log. The surge in file creation, flush, and archive activity collides with operating-system limits on file descriptors, asynchronous I/O contexts, and shared memory, causing kernel denials that further slow or block log operations. Each blocked flush extends transaction hold times, boosting in-memory log pressure and triggering even more checkpoints, which in turn amplifies I/O and resource requests to the OS. This feedback loop escalates until both the logging subsystem and the kernel resource pools are saturated, yielding a compounded performance and availability degradation characteristic of this composite anomaly.

entry.official_description: Incorrect parameter or combination of parameters for START REPLICA UNTIL
entry.cause_analysis: The failure is typically associated with log shipping, replica apply state, replication-channel configuration, or cross-node communication needed to keep replicated state consistent.
entry.solution_guidance: Inspect replication channel health, sender/receiver state, log retention, downstream apply lag, and network stability between replication endpoints.
